extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent agents preparing and filing PCT international applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and filing a PCT international application (request form, declarations, description, claims, drawings, sequence listings, signatures, and related procedural items). Intended to ensure compliance with PCT Rules and Annexes to maximise acceptance by designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of required wording and format for declarations (Section 214)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text must be used as set out in Section 214, no parts may be omitted or presented in an order different from that used in the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a declaration is furnished after the international filing date, the PCT application number must be added. Where there are several inventors, all inventors must sign and date a complete declaration containing all inventors (even if they do not sign the same copy), and the name, residence and address must be included for each inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized wording of declarations should be used
rubrics_metrics.description: The standardized wording should always be used otherwise the designated Offices may require the applicant to furnish a new declaration or further evidence in the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if published by the IB when non-standard wording is used, acceptance is up to each designated Office; applicants have no guarantee of acceptance. If standardized wording under Rule 4.17 is not applicable during international phase, consider complying during national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for declarations under Rule 4.17
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the declaration of inventorship for the purposes of designation of the United States of America must be signed and dated by all inventors. No other declaration must be signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that signature obligations vary by declaration type; check Rule 4.17 and Sections 214(a)/(b) for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Offices' acceptance of Rule 4.17 declarations depends on national requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All designated Offices that have special national requirements allowed under the PCT accept such declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the 'Special requirements of the Office' in the corresponding National Chapter (Summary) and National Phase paragraphs 5.003–5.005 for which States require substantive information in each declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated Offices may require further evidence only if veracity is reasonably doubted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the declaration is one of those in Rule 4.17(i)–(iv), the designated Office may not require documents or evidence relating to the subject matter unless it reasonably doubts the veracity of that declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For declarations under Rule 4.17(v) the designated Office may require further documents or evidence (e.g., matters of non-prejudicial disclosures and exceptions to lack of novelty are substantive patentability matters). A declaration itself does not establish the matters declared; matters remain for national determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations are published as part of the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: All declarations will be part of the published international application and will not be communicated separately to designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices will review declarations from the published application rather than receiving separate communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use check-boxes in Box No. VIII to correspond to declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The check-boxes in Box No. VIII should be completed by the applicant to allow the receiving Office to verify that the declarations referred to correspond to those made in Boxes No. VIII (i)–(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no declaration is made at filing or declarations are not yet available, do not include optional declaration sheets and leave the Box No. VIII check-boxes blank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or addition of declarations during international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration may be corrected, or a new (missing) declaration added, by a notice submitted to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rule 26ter.1 and paragraphs 6.045–6.050 for details. Note that a declaration may not be withdrawn once filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and completion of Box No. IX (Check List)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. IX should be completed by the applicant to allow the receiving Office to verify the completeness of the documents constituting and/or accompanying the international application and to check whether the application as filed actually contains the number of sheets in paper form indicated in items (a) to (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate the actual number of sheets for each element and the total. The request sheets are at least four (first, second, third, last) and may include optional sheets (continuation/supplemental/declaration). See paragraph 5.012 for numbering of sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate suggested drawing figure for abstract and filing language in Box No. IX
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must indicate in Box No. IX the number of the figure of the drawings (if any) suggested to accompany the abstract and preferably the language of filing of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps selection of an illustrative figure for publication and clarifies filing language; see paragraph 5.170 for abstract publication guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must sign the international application and signature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must be signed in Box No. X of the request by the applicant, or, where there are two or more applicants, by all of them. The receiving Office will not invite missing signatures when the request is signed by at least one applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Offices may require confirmation of the application by signature of any applicant who has not signed in accordance with national law. Subject to conditions (see paragraph 5.089), the request may be signed by the agent instead of the applicant(s). Multiple-applicant and agent-signature scenarios have specific power-of-attorney implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent may sign only if appointed by power of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application may be signed by an agent, but the agent must be appointed as such in a separate power of attorney signed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The power of attorney must be submitted to the receiving Office unless that Office waives the requirement. If a power of attorney is missing and the receiving Office requires it, the signature is treated as missing until the power is submitted. See paragraphs 5.041–5.051 and 11.001–11.014 for general power of attorney rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature execution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature should be executed indelibly in a dark color, preferably black ink, so that it will appear clearly in a photocopy. The name of each person signing should be indicated (preferably typewritten) next to the signature. Where signing on behalf of a legal entity, indicate capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use indelible dark ink, include typed name, and indicate capacity where relevant to avoid authenticity issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of seal instead of signature in certain receiving Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: In international applications filed with CNIPA (China), JPO (Japan) and MOIP (Republic of Korea) as receiving Office, a seal may be used instead of a signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check receiving Office-specific practice when using a seal in lieu of handwritten signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes to the request form are guidance only (not part of request)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notes to the request form are intended to facilitate completion; they indicate for each Box what indications are required and how to make them. The Notes are not required to be submitted with the request and should not be numbered as part of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Notes to avoid mistakes but do not include them as numbered sheets of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee calculation sheet recommended (not part of form)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee calculation sheet helps the applicant calculate total fees payable to the receiving Office. It is usually annexed to the request form but is not part of the form and is not counted as a sheet of the request; its use is not mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strongly recommended to complete and submit it to help the receiving Office verify calculations and identify errors. Indicate chosen International Searching Authority and applicable search fee amount if multiple authorities are competent. Refer to Notes to the fee calculation sheet for completion and paragraphs 5.184–5.199 for fee payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description must disclose invention sufficiently for skilled person (structure of description)
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art. It must start with the title of the invention and generally be in six parts with headings: 'Technical Field', 'Background Art', 'Disclosure of Invention', 'Brief Description of Drawings', 'Best Mode for Carrying Out the Invention' or 'Mode(s) for Carrying Out the Invention', and 'Industrial Applicability'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 5 contains detailed 'manner and order' requirements. Drafting with these parts will help acceptance by designated Offices and reduce need for national-phase amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider national practice when drafting description and best mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Details required for disclosure so the invention can be carried out depend on national Offices' practice; account for national practice (e.g., Japan, USA) when drafting. If a designated Office requires indication of best mode, that must be indicated in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapting description to national practice may avoid amendments during national phase. If at least one designated Office requires best mode (e.g., USPTO), include it in the description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing part must comply with WIPO Standard ST.26 (Annex C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence disclosure required to be in a sequence listing, the description must contain a sequence listing part complying with Annex C (WIPO Standard ST.26). Under ST.26 the sequence listing must be filed in XML format. Any language-dependent free text must be in a language accepted by the receiving Office; may be provided in English and another language if permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Annex C requirements for each receiving Office; see paragraphs 7.005–7.012 for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer electronic filing for applications containing sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application containing a sequence listing is best filed in electronic form since the sequence listing must be filed in XML format. The application should be filed in an electronic document format and/or by an accepted means of transmittal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Offices not accepting XML will transmit the application to the IB under Rule 19.4. Applicants are strongly discouraged from filing the main body on paper with the sequence listing separately in electronic form. For paper-filed applications the XML sequence listing must accompany the application (e.g., on electronic carrier).

rubrics_metrics.name: No page fees for XML sequence listings complying with ST.26
rubrics_metrics.description: No page fees are payable for any sequence listing filed in XML format in accordance with WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ST.26-compliant XML to avoid page fee charges associated with sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of non-XML electronic sequence files
rubrics_metrics.description: If a separate electronic file disclosing sequences is filed in a format other than XML, the receiving Office will invite the applicant to confirm whether the content should be added as sheets to the main description and, if necessary, resubmit in an accepted format. Some Offices may convert the file and ask confirmation. Sheets added will be taken into account for international filing fee calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may later amend the description to include an ST.26-compliant sequence listing. If applicant fails to confirm or pay applicable fees for sheets in excess of 30, the original content may be disregarded and not form part of the international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office acceptance of electronic sequence listings varies
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving Offices that accept filing of applications in electronic format are indicated in Annex C. Any receiving Office not accepting sequence listings in XML will transmit the application to the IB as receiving Office under Rule 19.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Annex C and receiving Office practice before filing sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO Sequence software recommended for ST.26 sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure compliance, sequence listings should be created using WIPO Sequence software (available from WIPO website).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using recommended software reduces non-compliance risks with ST.26/XML formatting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements for description (paper, margins, character size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper must be A4, white, durable. Minimum margins: 2 cm top, bottom and right; 2.5 cm left. Margins should not exceed 3 cm bottom/right and 4 cm top/left. Margins must be blank except for a file reference (<=25 characters) in the left-hand corner of top margin within 1.5 cm from top. File reference may use Latin letters and Arabic numerals; hyphen allowed. Any text matter must be in characters whose capital letters are not less than 0.28 cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with Rule 11 physical requirements to ensure acceptance; nonconforming sheets can cause issues with reproduction and filing formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page and line numbering and typing format
rubrics_metrics.description: Page number must be centered at top or bottom but not in the 2 cm margin. Strongly recommended that every fifth line be numbered in the right half of the left margin. Description must be typewritten/printed, 1½ spaced, in dark indelible color. Capital letters of characters must be minimum 0.28 cm high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper numbering and legible typeface facilitate reproduction and searching; follow Rules 11.7–11.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of chemical or mathematical formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulae may be written by hand or drawn if necessary but recommended to use drafting aids. Formulae may be grouped together on sheets and paginated with description; designate each formula by a reference sign and refer to them in the description. Formulae may also be placed after claims as drawings if complying with drawing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping formulae can be practical; ensure each formula is referenced in the description. When filed as drawings, comply with drawing requirements (paragraph 5.157 and Rules 11.10–11.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legibility, symbol use and sizing for formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical/mathematical formulae must employ symbols in general use and be completely unambiguous. Numerals, letters and signs not typed must be legible and identical in form across the application. In text, capital letters of symbols must be at least 0.28 cm; on drawing sheets at least 0.32 cm. Mathematical symbols should be explained in the description or collated in a list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency and legibility of symbols reduce ambiguity and examination burden; adhere to size minima depending on location (text vs drawings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation rules for tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables may be grouped on one or more sheets paginated with the description. If multiple tables, identify each by Roman numeral, capital letter, title, or other means. Each line and column should begin with an entry explaining what it represents and units if necessary. Tables should be set upright; if not possible, they may be placed sideways with top on left-hand side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 11.10(c)–(d) to ensure tables are clear and machine/reproduction-friendly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes in the description
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for rectification of obvious mistakes is explained under Rule 91. The omission of an entire sheet of the description cannot be rectified without affecting the international filing date. Changes other than rectification are considered amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to paragraphs 11.033–11.044 for rectification procedure. Avoid relying on rectification for missing entire sheets as it affects filing date and priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the description during the international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: The description can be amended during the international phase only if the applicant files a demand for international preliminary examination. The description can also be amended during the national phase before each designated or elected Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different provisions apply to amendment of the claims. Consider international preliminary examination (demand) timing if amendments to description are needed before national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must define protection sought, be clear, concise and supported
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim(s) must 'define the matter for which protection is sought.' Claims must be clear and concise and fully supported by the description. Claims should, whenever appropriate, be in two distinct parts: statement of prior art and statement of features for which protection is sought (characterizing portion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 6 for number/numbering, manner of claiming, dependent claims and two-part claim format when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple dependent claims rules and national differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PCT, a multiple dependent claim referring to more than one other claim must do so in the alternative only, and cannot serve as basis for another multiple dependent claim. However, many national laws permit different manner of claiming; use of different national style is permitted under PCT but may require amendments during national phase for States that do not permit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must decide drafting style with awareness that some International Searching Authorities may find meaningful search impossible and that national Offices may require claim adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application should be drafted so that the claims relate to only one invention or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept (Rule 13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity is important for international search and examination and affects fees if multiple inventions require separate searches/examinations. See paragraphs 7.015–7.021 and Annex B for detailed criteria and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for satisfying unity of invention (special technical features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity is present only when there is a technical relationship among claimed inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features. 'Special technical features' are those that define a contribution each claimed invention makes over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination is made without regard to how claims are phrased. Initial unity assessment (assuming claims avoid prior art) is made before search and may be reconsidered based on search results. Annex B contains detailed criteria and illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted combinations of different claim categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 13 permits inclusion of combinations such as (i) an independent claim for a product plus an independent claim for a process specially adapted to manufacture the product and a use claim; (ii) an independent claim for a process plus an independent claim for an apparatus specifically designed for carrying out the process; (iii) product + process + apparatus combinations where contributions correspond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A process is 'specially adapted' if it inherently results in the product; an apparatus is 'specifically designed' if its contribution over prior art corresponds to the process's contribution. Mere capability to be used in the process is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus considered specifically designed test
rubrics_metrics.description: An apparatus or means is considered specifically designed for carrying out a claimed process if the contribution over the prior art of the apparatus corresponds to the contribution the process makes over the prior art; mere capability to be used is insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft apparatus claims so their inventive contribution mirrors the process contribution when relying on combined-category unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush practice criteria for alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 13.2 governs Markush practice where a single claim defines alternatives. Technical interrelationship and same or corresponding special technical features are considered met when the alternatives are of a similar nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markush grouping acceptable particularly in chemical fields; assess similarity criteria carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Markush groupings of chemical compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When Markush grouping is for chemical compounds, alternatives are regarded as similar where (i) all alternatives have a common property or activity, and (ii) either (a) a common structure is present (a significant structural element is shared), or (b) if common structure cannot be unifying, all alternatives belong to a recognized class of compounds in the relevant art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at least one Markush alternative is found not novel, the examiner will reconsider unity though reconsideration does not automatically imply a lack of unity objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity criteria for intermediate and final products
rubrics_metrics.description: Intermediate and final products are considered to have unity where (i) they have the same essential structural element (basic chemical structures the same, or technically closely interrelated), and (ii) they are technically interrelated (final product manufactured directly from intermediate or separated by small number of intermediates containing same essential structural element).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity may be present even when structures are unknown provided sufficient evidence exists to conclude technical close interrelation (e.g., intermediate incorporates essential element into final product).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated/elected Offices must accept international applications complying with Rule 13
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application complying with unity requirements of Rule 13 must be accepted by all designated and elected Offices; Article 27(1) does not permit national laws to require different or additional contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complying with Rule 13 avoids inconsistent national-phase rejections on unity content grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements for claims (same as description) and claims start on new sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical requirements for claims are the same as for the description (paper, margins, type, character size). Claims must commence on a new sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims start on a new sheet and conform to Rule 11 physical requirements to avoid formality objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of tables in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may include tables if desirable, but tables must be included in the text of the relevant claim; they may not be annexed to the claims nor may reference be made to tables contained in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tables are used in claims, embed them directly in the claim text and format them per table presentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure under Rule 91 applies to rectification of obvious mistakes. Omission of an entire sheet of the claims cannot be rectified without affecting the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rectification request in claims is recommended only if mistake may affect the international search; otherwise amend the claims later. See paragraphs 11.033–11.044 for rectification procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of claims during international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be amended under Article 19 upon receipt of the international search report; they may also be amended during international preliminary examination if a demand is filed and during national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Article 19 amendments (post-ISR) and Article 34/10 procedures (if demand filed) appropriately to address objections prior to national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: When drawings must be included
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be included in the international application when they are necessary for the understanding of the invention. Applicants may include drawings even when not strictly necessary; any designated Office may require drawings during national phase if not filed initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include drawings if they aid understanding; omission may lead to national-phase requests to file drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of drawing (what counts as drawing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perspectives, exploded views, sections and cross-sections, details on different scales, flow sheets and diagrams (functional diagrams and graphic representations expressing relationships between parameters) are all considered drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure flowcharts, diagrams and graphical parameter plots are treated as drawings and comply with drawing requirements if included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between graphic forms and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical/mathematical formulae and tables included in the description, claims or abstract are not considered drawings and are not subject to drawing requirements; however, such graphic forms may be submitted as drawings, in which case they must comply with drawing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to file formulae/tables as part of text or as drawings depending on presentation needs and applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation requirements for drawings (separate sheets, minimal text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be presented on separate sheet(s) and may not be included in the description, claims or abstract. They may not contain text matter except a single word or words when absolutely indispensable. Any drawing meeting the drawing requirements must be accepted in the national phase by designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rules 11.10–11.13 for drawing content, and include file reference if desired. Drawings meeting PCT standards will obviate need for re-execution under national standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings must admit direct reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings must be presented so as to admit direct reproduction by photography, electrostatic processes, photo offset and microfilming, in any number of copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure high-contrast, clear lines and durable media so reproduction processes produce legible copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical requirements for drawing sheets (paper, margins, one side only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be on A4 sheets (29.7 x 21 cm), flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny and durable; free from creases/cracks; not folded. Each sheet must be reasonably free from erasures and alterations. Only one side may be used. Usable surface must not exceed 26.2 x 17.0 cm; sheets must not contain frames around usable surface. Minimum margins: top and left 2.5 cm; right 1.5 cm; bottom 1.0 cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict physical conformity facilitates reproduction and compliance; nonconforming drawing sheets risk formality objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of figures on drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures constituting the drawings must be grouped together on sheet(s) without waste of space but clearly separated from each other. Figures should not be separated by lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group figures to use space efficiently while keeping separation clear; avoid drawing separator lines between figures.
